events.title: Peter the Great Founds Saint Petersburg
events.description: During the Great Northern War, Tsar Peter I founded a new city on the Neva River, on land recently taken from Sweden. He meant it to be Russia's 'window on the West'.
events.significance: Saint Petersburg became the Russian capital and a center of art, politics and trade. It shaped Russia's turn toward Europe.

events.title: Battle of Tsushima Begins
events.description: In the Russo-Japanese War, Japan's fleet engaged the Russian Baltic Fleet in the Tsushima Strait. The Russian fleet had sailed halfway around the world to get there.
events.significance: Japan's decisive naval victory stunned the world. It showed that an Asian power could defeat a European one, and it hastened the end of the war.

events.title: Birth of Henry Kissinger
events.description: Henry Kissinger was born in Germany. He later emigrated to the United States and became a Harvard scholar. He served as National Security Advisor and Secretary of State.
events.significance: Kissinger was a leading figure in Cold War diplomacy, including the opening to China and détente with the Soviet Union.

events.title: Golden Gate Bridge Opens to Pedestrians
events.description: The suspension bridge linking San Francisco with Marin County opened to the public. It was the longest main span in the world at the time.
events.significance: The bridge became one of the most recognized landmarks in the world and a symbol of American engineering.
